title: Review: one-choice problems
idea: GUIDED review of the whole unit: comparisons, if/else, one-sided choices, and the UEPCC habit, plus a fresh tiny problem.
problem: Review of deciding between two outcomes, end-to-end with UEPCC.

exercises.prompt: PROBLEM: a parking fee is 0 for under 15 minutes, else 5. The OUTPUT is...
exercises.explanation: Output is one fee value. Name it first.

exercises.prompt: By hand: minutes = 10 gives what fee?
exercises.explanation: 10 is under 15, so the fee is 0.

exercises.prompt: By hand: minutes = 30 gives what fee?
exercises.explanation: 30 is not under 15, so the fee is 5.
'Under' is strictly less, so < 15. Exactly 15 is NOT under 15.
Compare, branch to set the fee, then print it.
Set fee inside the matching branch, then print it.

exercises.prompt: Run with minutes = 10. What does print(fee) show?
exercises.explanation: 10 < 15 is True, so fee = 0 - matches the hand example.

exercises.prompt: Re-check the edge: minutes = 15. What prints?
exercises.explanation: 15 < 15 is False, so the else runs: fee = 5. The edge confirms < was correct.

exercises.prompt: if/else always runs exactly one of its two branches - never both, never neither.
exercises.explanation: Right. With an else, one path always runs and only one. That is the two-outcome choice.

exercises.prompt: After this unit you can confidently solve which kind of problem?
options: Decide between two outcomes using a comparison
exercises.explanation: Two-outcome decisions are solid now. Many buckets (elif) and more conditions come in the next units.
